title: Dust fits to three CPV nights need an 8.0 to 9.6 percent color correction within one quoted error
abstract: We test the shared stellar color assumption in dust fits to 11 published depths of TIC 262400835 on three nights. At nominal wavelengths and opacity index 2, an analytic inequality requires a fixed relative depth correction of at least 7.98 percent to fit all depths within one quoted marginal error. An explicit finite-column screen fits with 9.53 percent. Restricting coverage to five percent of r-band brightness permits a 10.03 percent correction. The central depths require at least 14.60 percent. Linear relaxation and finite-column fits bracket the continuum problem. These are feasibility bounds, not a statistical confidence interval or evidence for a measured stellar color anomaly. Physical stellar spectra, real filter responses and dip geometry were not fitted. Original code, aggregate witness models, proof and source hashes are supplied.

display.caption: Necessary lower bounds and feasible upper bounds on the fixed color correction. Missing feasible points are grid failures, not continuum exclusions.
